summary.text: Ben Hocking is the Greens candidate for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian election. His job is in surveillance, a field where he also acts as a union delegate, and he was previously a journalist. He describes himself as a long-time local and says he decided to stand over planning decisions and public transport in the area.

priorities.text: A stronger anti-corruption body and more transparency in politics
Workers' rights
More GPs and better funding for the local hospital
Better train services for the area
Public education, the local environment and social justice

sources.title: Williamstown: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Ben Hocking, Candidate for Williamstown, Australian Greens

priorities.text: Support for families and children
More parental choice in education
Housing and infrastructure planned ahead of population growth
Accountable, transparent government
Reducing state debt and cost-of-living pressures

summary.text: Bruce O'Regan is the Family First candidate for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. His party page says he has worked in engineering design and project management for more than 25 years and lives with his wife in Strathmore, where they attend a Baptist church. He grew up in Melbourne's eastern suburbs.

summary.text: Catherine Loughnan is One Nation's candidate for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC she has been in business for close to 40 years, now in transport and logistics, has owned small businesses and has been a resident of Melbourne's west for 45 years. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

sources.title: Williamstown: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Gill Gannon is the West Party candidate for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian election. She runs an interior decorating business, is president of the Newport Traders Association and says she led the local campaign against closing Champion Road. She says she has lived, worked and brought up her family in Melbourne's inner west.

priorities.text: Keeping Champion Road open
Making sure state decisions take account of the people of the west

sources.title: Williamstown: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Gill Gannon, The West Party for Williamstown

summary.text: Melissa Horne has held Williamstown for Labor since 2018 and became a minister straight after her first election, starting with public transport and ports and freight. She has since had portfolios including roads and road safety, local government and health infrastructure, and since August 2026 has been minister for jobs, industry and advanced manufacturing, and defence industry, as well as ports and freight. She is recontesting Williamstown in 2026.

summary.text: Oskar Martin is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian election. A Bundjalung and Kamilaroi man born in Broken Hill, he moved to Williamstown while in primary school. He works in university research, is a member of the National Tertiary Education Union and has campaigned for Aboriginal and Palestinian rights.

occupation.note: The party page says he is a research assistant in the Aboriginal History Archive at Victoria University; the ABC says he works in mental health research at the University of Melbourne.

priorities.text: Land rights and an end to Aboriginal deaths in custody and high incarceration rates
Secure housing and welfare payments people can live on
Free, publicly owned health and education services
put people before profits

sources.title: Williamstown: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Oskar Martin, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Paul Lindemann is the Liberal candidate for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian election. He grew up in Altona, has spent his life in Melbourne's west and has run a business in the area for more than two decades. The party's page also points to his involvement in local sport and community groups.

priorities.text: Safer communities
Better local infrastructure
Lower living costs

summary.text: Sagar Reddy Yarra is the candidate of The Republican (registered as The Republican Make Australia Great Again) for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. The party was registered in Victoria in September 2026. Neither the party nor the ABC had published a biography of him as at 9 Nov 2026.

summary.text: Tony Briffa is standing as an independent for Williamstown at the 2026 Victorian election. Born in Altona, Briffa was elected to Hobsons Bay City Council in 2008 and served as deputy mayor and then mayor, a term that Wikipedia says made her the first openly intersex mayor known anywhere. Her working life has included jobs with Defence and the federal police, and she has long advocated for intersex people's rights.

occupation.text: Has worked for the Department of Defence, the Australian Federal Police and Ambulance Victoria's aviation provider
